headline: High: shared filesystem/git writes from Claude Code can conflict with Pathway workflows; other risks are limited by Pathway's no-IO profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read/write repo files and use MCP, while Pathway has no filesystem or MCP surfaces. A prompt-injection path exists only if the operator manually bridges Claude Code outputs into Pathway inputs or shared files; Pathway itself does not ingest Claude Code by default. The blast radius is limited to the bridged document/workflow.
conditions: IF the operator copies Claude Code output into a Pathway pipeline input file or prompt field.
IF a shared filesystem artifact is later parsed by Pathway as instructions.
mitigations: Keep Pathway inputs read-only from Claude Code outputs.
Use separate directories for Claude Code and Pathway artifacts.
Add a manual review step before any Pathway ingestion.
Disable MCP connectors that forward Claude Code text into Pathway.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and secrets, but Pathway exposes no filesystem, network, or API egress in its profile. Leakage requires an unusual bridge such as exporting Claude Code artifacts into Pathway inputs; Pathway is not documented to receive those data classes directly. The pairwise risk is therefore small and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF Claude Code outputs containing secrets are written into a Pathway-ingested file.
IF Pathway is configured to process the same directory that Claude Code uses for working files.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in shared working directories.
Separate code repos from Pathway ingestion paths.
Redact secrets before any handoff.
Review Pathway inputs for sensitive fields before processing.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filters at the handoff boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code has broad filesystem and git write capabilities and shares state via filesystem and git only; Pathway is non-runnable here and has no write capabilities. The conflict is one-sided but real if Pathway is used to generate or transform files that Claude Code also edits, creating overlapping mutable resources. Uncertainty about Pathway's runtime integration pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Pathway writes to a directory that Claude Code also edits.
IF both agents modify the same git working tree without external locking.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Have only one agent own git commits.
Run a quick diff before merging outputs.
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can produce code or file changes that Pathway may consume as downstream inputs, but Pathway has no documented verification or critical-evaluation surface in the profile. If Pathway treats Claude Code output as authoritative, errors can cascade into multiple work products. Because the interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, medium is the higher defensible choice.
conditions: IF Pathway ingests files generated by Claude Code without validation.
IF Claude Code output is used as a source of truth for downstream processing.
mitigations: Insert a human review gate before ingestion.
Validate schemas and checksums on handoff.
Keep generated artifacts separate from source-of-truth data.
Require Pathway to consume only signed or reviewed inputs.
requires-engineering: add automated verification between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code explicitly handles git credentials and local source code, while Pathway's profile shows no data classes, residency, or retention commitments. No direct compliance breach is evidenced, but the mismatch is that Claude Code may process sensitive local development data while Pathway's compliance posture is undocumented. The other agent is not cited beyond its lack of relevant controls.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into a Pathway workflow that lacks documented retention controls.
IF Claude Code secrets are exported into a Pathway-managed dataset.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair unless documented controls exist.
Document retention and deletion expectations before use.
Avoid exporting credentials or tokens into shared artifacts.
Review access logs for any regulated fields.
requires-engineering: obtain compliance documentation for Pathway.
